Title: Nepal’s Brain Drain wont STOP. Here’s what to do NEXT
Description:
The narrative across Nepal right now is clear: staying here feels like losing out on opportunities. Every day, thousands of Nepalis leave, most of them from the working class. It’s easy to think this migration is a problem we need to stop. But here’s the truth: migration of this nature has never stopped anywhere in the world.

So, what do we do next? Instead of fighting the inevitable, we need to embrace the power of the Nepali diaspora. By creating stronger connections with Nepalis abroad, we can explore how their skills, investments, and networks can benefit Nepal.
That said, while the diaspora has the potential to help, it’s not inherently so. How can we ensure their involvement truly uplifts Nepal? Watch the video to understand the opportunities and the challenges of turning migration into a force for positive change.

Title: Why Nepal is so CORRUPT ?
Description:
Dive deep into the hidden mechanisms behind corruption in Nepal, exploring how systemic flaws, psychological factors, and societal norms perpetuate unethical practices. In this video, we break down the key concepts of corruption through the lens of:

Psychology of Corruption – Discover how individual beliefs, motivations, and moral justifications drive corrupt behavior and create a cycle that is tough to break.

Principal-Agent Theory – Understand the misalignment of incentives between those in power (agents) and the citizens they represent (principals). We’ll show how this gap fosters a culture where personal gain overshadows public service.

Collective Action Problem – Learn why collective efforts to fight corruption often fail, and how lack of trust, coordination, and mutual accountability keep honest citizens on the sidelines.

Role of Society – See how cultural values, social expectations, and daily interactions contribute to normalized corruption, making it more complex to eradicate.

By unraveling these interconnected factors, we aim to spark critical thinking and open up a conversation on the necessary reforms and mindset shifts. Join us to examine what keeps corruption alive—and what it will take to truly break the cycle in Nepal.

Description:
Lead poisoning has become a critical, yet overlooked issue in Nepal. Despite government guidelines limiting lead content in products like paint, many manufacturers are neglecting these regulations, using dangerously high levels of lead. This puts millions of Nepali people—especially children—at serious risk. Lead exposure can cause devastating health effects, including developmental issues in children, kidney damage, and even death.

In this video, we dive into the alarming rise of lead poisoning in Nepal, the industries responsible, and the shocking reality of how widespread this problem could soon become. With so few people aware of the dangers, it’s more important than ever to shed light on this issue and push for stronger enforcement of regulations. Join us as we explore how this hidden threat is putting the entire country at risk and what we can do to help protect our communities.

Title: Nepal's Failing International Airport Projects
Description:
Expectations were sky-high when Nepal opened two new international airports in Pokhara and Bhairahawa. The government took on heavy loans from China to build the Pokhara International Airport as well as a loan from the Asian Development Bank for Gautam Buddha International Airport, hoping to attract tourists and foreign investment. Now the country struggles to repay the massive loans while the airports remain largely unused. A classic case of how big dreams, mismanagement, and China's debt trap diplomacy led Nepal's impressive new infrastructure to the brink of failure.

Title: Why Nepal might get hit by a Massive Earthquake Soon?
Description:
For nearly 500 years, the western region of Nepal has not experienced a major earthquake. However, geologists warn that the area is overdue for a massive quake that could cause significant damage and loss of life. According to experts, stress has been building up in the fault lines under western Nepal, putting the region at high risk of a catastrophic event. Despite these warnings, many Nepalis remain skeptical and unprepared. While some dismiss the warnings as a hoax, the scientific data shows that western Nepal could experience an earthquake magnitude 7.  or higher in the coming decades. With more than two-thirds of buildings in the region constructed of non-earthquake resistant materials, experts warn that the impact would be devastating without significant preparation and investment in disaster readiness. Nepali officials would be wise to take this threat seriously, inform and prepare citizens, and put measures in place to minimize damage and save lives when an earthquake does inevitably hit western Nepal.

Title: Why NEPAL needs a NEW CAPITAL CITY?
Description:
Nepal's current capital city of Kathmandu is facing serious challenges that are impeding the country's progress. Kathmandu's population has grown rapidly in recent decades, straining the city's infrastructure and resources. Traffic congestion, pollution, overcrowding and rising housing costs have become the norm. The city's vulnerability to natural disasters like earthquakes  further illustrate the need for a new, more sustainable capital. A new capital city could be better designed to meet Nepal's needs for the 21st century and beyond. It could provide an opportunity for economic growth beyond tourism and alleviate some of the pressures facing Kathmandu. While changing a capital city is a complex endeavor, the current problems afflicting Kathmandu strongly suggest that Nepal should seriously consider this option to help build a more prosperous and livable nation for future generations. So, is it time Nepal adopts a new Capital City?
